title: Level 5 (World Class) - C-14
notes:
West leads the ♣A against 5♦. West wins the first trick as East encourages and West's shift to the ♠4 is taken by South with the ♠A. West's opening lead and his shift to an unusual spade spot strongly suggest that East was dealt 4 clubs headed by the ♣Q10. In this case South will require an endplay to succeed.

South finesses in hearts. It is OK to draw 1 round of trump first, but West must have the ♥K for the contract to have a chance. Dummy's remaining spade (with a high trump) to eliminate that suit. A heart is played to dummy's ♥A and a heart is ruffed high as East discards a spade. South then draws 2 rounds of trump ending in the dummy.

If both defenders follow to 2 rounds of diamonds North's heart is led and South can choose which of the defenders he wants to endplay (alternatively South can lead the ♣J or ♣9 from dummy to endplay East at once). South can either ruff dummy's last heart and duck a club to endplay East, or South can discard a club on dummy's last heart allowing West to win the trick. West will be endplayed in this variation, forced to concede a ruff and discard.

If West discards on the second round of diamonds, dummy's ♦9 wins and the last heart is played, catching East in an unusual 3-suit squeeze. If East discards a club, South will ruff and give up a club trick to East before drawing his last trump. If instead East ruffs when dummy's last heart is played, South can overruff and duck a club to endplay East. Note that dummy's third diamond is vital for this endplay to come off (as it prevents East's spade from being a safe exit card).

Finally, if East discards his last spade on the 4th round of hearts, South can ruff and draw East's last trump. With both dummy and East down to just 3 clubs, a club to the ♣9 or ♣J will endplay East.
